checks.value: checked: TOIs, CTOIs, confirmed planets, TESS EB catalog, AAVSO VSX, Gaia DR3 eclipsing binaries and orbits

checks.name: Period recovery
checks.detail: the dip is 2.7 h from where the search put it, and 36.8 ppt deep there (found at 16.3 ppt): repeats are sought at that depth; found the 36.8 ppt transit 1 more time in TESS (BTJD 2162.10; same depth and duration, above the 7.0σ false-alarm threshold); the dips don't fit one period without predicting a transit where TESS saw none: not one transiting body, or the repeats are something else; ASAS-SN sees the transit at P 415.6802 d: 92.4 ppt ± 9.04 ppt in 2 transits (4 points, Δχ² 105); one TESS transit, so the period-based TESS checks still can't run, but it's predicted
checks.value: 16 sectors scanned (353 d): BTJD 2162.10, 31.4 ppt, SNR 17.9 · ATLAS not used (needs an ATLAS_API_TOKEN) · 3983 ASAS-SN points over 11.1 yr · 22% of 10.5-2000 d allowed by the TESS coverage, ASAS-SN rules out 6% of those

checks.name: Individual transits
checks.detail: one TESS transit: the period (416 d) comes from ZTF alone
checks.value: BTJD 2155.45 (sector 31, SPOC): vetting SNR 8.5, 36.8 ppt (the search's SNR was 9.8: a different detrending, binning and noise estimate)

checks.name: Engineering data
checks.detail: no transit falls in a known engineering interval

checks.name: Raw flux (SAP)
checks.detail: the dip is in the raw aperture flux too, not made by the detrending
checks.value: 1 transit: pipeline flux 41.2 ppt ± 8.54, raw SAP 29.8 ppt ± 4.57 (expected 31 ppt after SPOC's crowding correction, CROWDSAP 0.75); s31 SPOC

checks.name: Background correlation
checks.detail: the dip doesn't follow the pipeline's background estimate
checks.value: raw SAP 29.8 ppt ± 4.57; with the background regressed out 29.8 ppt ± 4.53; flux-background correlation |r| 0.07 within ±1.5 d

checks.name: Event consistency
checks.detail: compares transits with each other: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Signal uniqueness (single event)
checks.detail: a brightening at BTJD 2156.32 is also above the false-alarm threshold: the systematics make events this size in both directions
checks.value: the dip 50.6σ white, 50.6σ red (F_red 1.00 from 632 box positions over 337 d); threshold 4.2σ (noise reaches it anywhere in that much data 1% of the time); strongest brightening 9.5σ red at BTJD 2156.32

checks.name: SNR growth
checks.detail: how the SNR builds over transits: a periodic signal only

checks.name: Period consistency
checks.detail: one transit: there's no period to check (the alias and shape checks bound it instead)

checks.name: Alias periods
checks.detail: periods under 10.5 d would have shown a second transit in the data around the dip

checks.name: Detrending sensitivity
checks.detail: the depth changes by more than 30% with local quadratic 1.67 d
checks.value: running median 0.83 d: 27.5 ppt (SNR 6.4); running median 1.33 d: 36.7 ppt (SNR 8.4); running median 2.33 d: 41 ppt (SNR 9.4); local quadratic 1.67 d: 25.1 ppt (SNR 9.1)

checks.name: Depth stability
checks.detail: one transit: nothing to compare its depth with (the pipeline and detrending checks test it instead)

checks.name: Odd/even depths
checks.detail: one transit: there are no alternate transits to compare

checks.name: Secondary eclipse
checks.detail: another significant dip at BTJD 2162.01 (30% of the depth): a secondary eclipse of a binary, or a second transit
checks.value: deepest other dip: BTJD 2162.01, 10.9 ppt (21.2σ red); in raw SAP 18.8 ppt ± 2.65, background regressed out 19.7 ppt; limit for an eclipse anywhere in 337 d of data: 1.03 ppt (3σ red)

checks.name: Transit shape
checks.detail: SNR 8.5 is too low to tell a V from a U

checks.name: Duration vs expected
checks.detail: no period and no stellar density

checks.name: Period from the transit shape
checks.detail: no catalog density

checks.name: Variability at the transit period
checks.detail: the star varies (out of transit)
checks.value: P 11.2 d, 4.78 ppt (significant in 1 of 8 sectors)

checks.name: Pulsation removal
checks.detail: the transit survives subtracting the star's pulsations, at the same depth
checks.value: 31 periodic signals removed: 59.1 h (3.64 ppt), 42.5 h (3.57 ppt), 49.5 h (2.66 ppt), 15.1 h (2.06 ppt), 67.8 h (2.03 ppt); transit 36.8 ppt (SNR 8.5) → 33.5 ppt (SNR 8.6), 8 sectors

checks.name: Archival radial velocities
checks.detail: no archival RVs: Gaia DR3 has no RV time series for the star (too faint or too hot for RVS); not in APOGEE DR17

checks.name: Centroid shift
checks.detail: no significant centroid motion: the source is within ~3″ of the target (3σ)
checks.value: 2 sectors; implied source offset 1.0 ± 0.7″ (shift 0.9σ)

checks.name: Difference imaging
checks.detail: ran on 1 sector, but no source visible in the pixels (0.2σ): the transit is too shallow for TESS's full-frame images; it can't say which star dims
checks.value: s31: 1 transits, source 0.2σ

checks.name: Own pixel photometry
checks.detail: the dip is in our own photometry of the pixels, with the background removed per column: not a pipeline artifact
checks.value: s31: 36.6 ppt ± 5.58 with column-wise background, 37.3 ppt ± 5.34 without; pipeline 41.2 ppt ± 8.54 at the same transits (expected here ~32.9 ppt)

checks.name: Detector position
checks.detail: well inside the CCD
checks.value: no dead row or column in the cutout

checks.name: Aperture growth
checks.detail: the dip keeps its depth in a bigger aperture: light lost, not moved by a blurred PSF
checks.value: s31: r 1 px (2 px) 41.3 ppt ± 6.15, r 3 px (28 px) 27.5 ppt ± 4.2; expected in the large one from the neighbours' dilution 27.9 ppt

checks.name: Pointing jitter
checks.detail: no extra pointing jitter during the dip

checks.name: Aperture dependence
checks.detail: large/small depth ratio 1.02 (0.0σ). Not scored: QLP's 1x1 and 5x5 px apertures aren't dilution-corrected, and known on-target planets differ by up to 3x too; a pixel-level (TPF) test is needed
checks.value: small -0.701 ppt ± 0.346, large -0.716 ppt ± 0.568 (QLP, 1 sector)

checks.name: Nearby sources
checks.detail: the pixel and centroid tests rule out 26 of them; the rest are over 1′ away
checks.value: 26 of 2999 Gaia DR3 stars within 2′ could cause a 36.8 ppt dip if eclipsed: Gaia 4657168592571185536 at 16″, T 15.4 (needs a 69% eclipse); Gaia 4657168553995939200 at 19″, T 15.2 (needs a 62% eclipse); Gaia 4657168553875023360 at 23″, T 14.2 (needs a 26% eclipse); Gaia 4657168592571181184 at 36″, T 15.0 (needs a 50% eclipse)

checks.name: Unresolved companions
checks.detail: Gaia sees no companion beyond ~1″ (9951 au at 9951 pc), and RUWE 0.86 disfavours bright ones at ~0.1-1″; closer than ~0.5-1″ (4975 au at 9951 pc) only speckle/AO imaging can look (the statistical validation below allows for them)
checks.value: RUWE 0.86 · 2 Gaia sources within 4″: 3.0″ ΔG 6.2, 3.0″ ΔG 7.6
